newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway billionaire says buys 6 pct in Storebrand.
newsitem.headline: Norway billionaire says buys 6 pct in Storebrand.

text.p: Norwegian billionaire entrepreneur Kjell Inge Roekke said on Friday he had bought around six percent of the ordinary shares in Norway's largest insurance company Storebrand ASA.
In a statement, Roekke said the stock was purchased through his private Liberian-registered company Ivory Enterprises Corp.

Brokers on the Oslo bourse reported last week that there was a huge demand for Storebrand shares. The company's share price has risen from 42.50 crowns on February 25 to 46.80 crowns at the close on Thursday.

Roekke is the largest shareholder in Norwegian industrial holding company Aker RGI ASA, which was established last year after his former company Resource Group International (RGI) merged with engineering and construction group Aker ASA .

"The acquisition is a long-term investment," Roekke said in a statement. "A significant part of the shares are bought from foreign investors and the acquisition means that Storebrand will remain in Norwegian hands."
Roekke said he hoped the acquisition would contribute to a stable ownership structure in Storebrand and he emphasised that his main business activities were focused on Aker RGI.
Storebrand's share stood 0.80 crowns down at 0921 GMT at 46 crowns.
